overtime-calculator.metaDescription: Calculate overtime pay instantly. Enter your hourly rate, regular and overtime hours and the OT multiplier (e.g. 1.5x) to get gross pay. Free & private.
overtime-calculator.keywords: overtime calculator, ot pay calculator, overtime pay, time and a half calculator
overtime-calculator.quickAnswer: Overtime pay = overtime hours x hourly rate x multiplier. For example, at $20/hour with 5 overtime hours at 1.5x: regular pay is 40 x 20 = $800, overtime is 5 x 20 x 1.5 = $150, and gross pay is $950. Change the multiplier for double-time or custom rules.
keyFacts: Overtime pay rewards hours beyond the standard schedule at a premium rate, commonly 1.5x ('time and a half').
The multiplier is set by contract or law: 1.5x is typical, 2x ('double time') applies on some holidays.
Regular pay and overtime pay are calculated separately, then added for gross pay.
This tool works in any currency - enter your rate in whatever currency you are paid.
Gross pay here is before tax and deductions; take-home pay is always lower.
howTo: Enter your hourly rate in your currency.
Enter your regular hours for the period (often 40 per week).
Set the multiplier - 1.5 for time-and-a-half, 2 for double time.
Read your regular pay, overtime pay and gross pay instantly.
overtime-calculator.formula:
Regular pay = regular hours x hourly rate.
Overtime rate = hourly rate x multiplier.
Overtime pay = overtime hours x overtime rate.
Gross pay = regular pay + overtime pay.
Example: 40 x 20 = 800; 5 x (20 x 1.5) = 150; total = 950.
overtime-calculator.workedExample:
Rate $20/h, 40 regular hours, 5 OT hours, 1.5x multiplier.
1. Regular: 40 x 20 = $800.
2. OT rate: 20 x 1.5 = $30/h.
3. Overtime: 5 x 30 = $150.
4. Gross: 800 + 150 = $950.
With double time (2x): overtime = 5 x 40 = $200, gross = $1,000.
benefits: Verify your payslip in seconds - know exactly what you should earn.
Compare job offers with different overtime rules on equal terms.
Handles any multiplier, from 1.25x weekend rates to 3x holiday rates.
Private: salary numbers never leave your browser.
limitations: Gross pay is before tax, insurance and other deductions - not take-home pay.
No currency is assumed; make sure your rate matches the currency you expect.
Does not model tiered rules (for example, 1.5x for the first 2 hours then 2x) - use the blended multiplier.
This is an estimate, not legal or payroll advice; your employer's rules decide.

faqs.q: What does 1.5x (time and a half) mean?
faqs.a: You earn your normal hourly rate plus half again for each overtime hour. At $20/hour, overtime pays $30/hour.
Often on public holidays or after very long shifts, depending on contract or law. Set the multiplier to 2 to model it.
None specifically - it is currency-agnostic. Enter your rate in dollars, rupees, riyals or anything else and read the result in the same currency.
No. Gross pay is before income tax, social contributions and deductions. Your payslip's net figure will be lower.

faqs.q: Can I use weekly or monthly hours?
faqs.a: Yes - the math is period-agnostic. Just keep regular hours, overtime hours and rate in the same period.

faqs.q: What if my overtime has two different rates?
faqs.a: Run the tool twice - once per rate - and add the two overtime amounts together.
